attributes.text: An account: the resource pyrite.dev/Account, whose principals are user:<id>.
EMAIL, PHONE or USERNAME.
The address, the number in E.164, or the username, as Pyrite normalized it.
Whether the account prefers it among its identifiers; the caller sets it.
An identifier of an account: the resource pyrite.dev/Identifier, under its account.
PENDING while it is enrolled, then ACTIVE.

The password's Argon2id hash, the TOTP secret encrypted, the passkey's credential, the recovery codes' MACs, or the
provider account as its sign-in proved it.

A passkey's credential id, or the provider and the id of a provider account, as google:1093...; empty for the
others.
A passkey's signature counter, or the last TOTP step that signed in.
Whether a passkey verified its user when it was registered.
A factor of an account: the resource pyrite.dev/Factor, under its account.
A session of an account: the resource pyrite.dev/Session, under its account.
The factor.
The name of the provider in the options, such as google.
The id of the account at the provider.

The account at a provider that a factor of the kind PROVIDER links. The provider and the id are unique together, so
that no account at a provider is linked to two accounts. It goes with its factor.
The id of the token, before the dot in the token.
The session.
The MAC of the token's secret, which the MAC key of the options signs.
When a refresh traded the token for the next; unset while it works.

A refresh token of a session. A refresh trades it for the next, so a token works once; one that comes back after its
trade ends its session. It goes with its session.
The account; unset for an exchange that names no account that exists.
The identifier that the exchange started with, if any.
The stage of the definition that the exchange is in.
What the answers of the stage have proven, as JSON.

The random nonce of the stage, which a passkey answer signs, and when it, and what the verifiers keep with it, stop
working.

What the verifiers keep for the stage, such as the MAC of the code that was sent, as JSON by the name of the
answer.
The factor that the exchange enrolls, if any.
The id of the last answer's request, and the exchange that it returned.
Whether the exchange is done; a done exchange takes no answers.
The account at a provider that the exchange creates an account for, as a ProviderAccount.
An exchange in progress. It is not a resource: only the Authentication service reads and writes it.
The pyrite.schema.v1.Declaration, serialized.
The OpenFGA store of the grants.
The authorization model that the declaration wrote to the store.

A declaration that pyrite.schema.v1.Schema wrote, with the OpenFGA store and model that it wrote for it. The latest
is the one that every service reads.
The resource's name, such as projects/ledger.
The declared type, such as acme.dev/Project.
The name of the resource it is under; unset for a resource at the top.

A resource that Pyrite knows: its type and the resource it is under. The application keeps the resource itself;
Pyrite keeps where it sits, so that grants reach it from its parents and nothing is made twice.
How often the key gets a new primary version, in seconds; 0 for never.
When the key next gets a new primary version, if it rotates.
The name of the version that encrypts and signs.
A key: the resource pyrite.dev/Key, with the standard fields and its own.
1 for the first version of the key, and one more for each after it.
The public key of a signing version, as a JWK; empty for the others.
The key material, encrypted by the root key.
The X.509 SubjectPublicKeyInfo of a signing version; empty for the others.
A version of a key: the resource pyrite.dev/KeyVersion, under its key.
